reviewer: Independent second opinion: geographic facts and player-facing wording
judgment: No confirmed false assigned geographic claim was established within this review's checked scope. The current bank needs a wording pass before an unconditional player-facing sign-off: the Europe-neighbour clue assigned to Mongolia and North Korea hides a whole-country classification rule, and the Pacific-coast clue should state that marginal seas count. Alphabet-half conditions fit the user's requested basic, mildly wicked general hints; any wording polish there is optional.
independence: Earlier accuracy-review.json and fairness-review.json reports were not consulted. The current bank, including its source and explanatory notes, was read; findings were formed from actual assignments, fresh official tables/data and targeted primary sources.

scope.coverage: Full bank/runtime membership and wording scan; 77 assigned land-neighbour-area calculations; 25 UN M49 catalog membership sets; fresh World Bank 2023 land-area comparison for all 194 covered answer countries; targeted primary geography research in the listed cases. Border graphs and every island/coast were not independently reconstructed for all 195 countries.
excludedWork: No app, bank, gameplay, source or exported hints were changed.
No earlier accuracy/fairness verdict was used.
No full population audit or playtesting was performed.

findings.text: Has a land neighbour in Europe.
findings.problem: Mongolia borders Russia and China. Russia is in Europe under the bank's UN M49 country grouping, but Mongolia's actual Russian boundary lies in Asian Russia. A player can reasonably read the hint as saying that a neighbouring land area is in Europe. The short text hides the country-wide classification rule, so formal membership alone is not a satisfactory player-facing sign-off.

evidence.title: National Digital Atlas of Mongolia
evidence.supports: Places Mongolia in the Asian continent and lists only China and Russia as border states.

evidence.title: UN M49 geographic table
evidence.supports: Groups the Russian Federation in Eastern Europe and Mongolia in Eastern Asia.

findings.suggestedPlainLanguageRemedy: If preserving this relation, say “Borders a country with land in Europe.” A clearer alternative for Mongolia is “Has exactly two land neighbours.” Recheck assignments and candidate counts before changing the bank.

findings.text: Has a land neighbour in Europe.
findings.problem: North Korea's neighbours are China, South Korea and Russia. The European match is Russia as a whole; the shared boundary is on the Russian Far East side of East Asia. The current phrase invites the reasonable but wrong inference that North Korea is next to Europe. This is a scope/wording problem rather than a demonstrated false claim under the stored M49 definition.

findings.suggestedPlainLanguageRemedy: If preserving this relation, say “Borders a country with land in Europe.” Otherwise choose a straightforward geography or land-area clue after checking the answer pool.

findings.problem: Cambodia's coast is on the Gulf of Thailand. South Korea, also assigned this phrase, has coasts on the surrounding Pacific seas. These are defensible Pacific-basin memberships, but “Has a Pacific coast.” does not say that nearby seas count. The Indian Ocean clue explicitly says “or its seas”, making the convention inconsistent and inviting direct-ocean interpretations. The evidence confirms the memberships; it does not establish that the literal short wording is unambiguous.

findings.suggestedPlainLanguageRemedy: Use “Has a coast on the Pacific Ocean or its seas.” Apply the same ocean-coast convention consistently.

findings.text: Has a coast on the Indian Ocean or its seas.
findings.problem: Jordan's sea access is through the Gulf of Aqaba and Red Sea. The current phrase already allows the Indian Ocean's seas, and FAO explicitly includes Jordan, Israel, Egypt and the Persian Gulf states in the relevant region. It is defensible and more explicit than the Pacific phrase. A player still has to know which small seas belong to the basin; the named-sea clue would be more direct for the Red Sea cases.

evidence.supports: Defines its scope to include the Red Sea and Persian Gulf and lists Jordan, Israel, Egypt, Bahrain, Iraq, Kuwait and Qatar.

findings.suggestedPlainLanguageRemedy: Keep the existing explicit scope, or use the catalog's “Has a Red Sea or Gulf of Aden coast.” for suitable Red Sea countries after checking candidate counts. No factual correction is established here.

findings.text: First letter is not in the second half of the alphabet.
findings.problem: The two actual assignments, Argentina and Indonesia, use a negative alphabet-half condition. This fits the user's explicit suggestion and is an accepted basic, mildly wicked general hint. An affirmative A–M formulation may read faster, but the negative form is not a player-preference violation.

evidence.title: Current bank assignments
evidence.supports: This exact phrase is assigned only to AR and ID. The user explicitly proposed a negative alphabet-half condition; the clearer formulation is an optional editorial judgment.

findings.suggestedPlainLanguageRemedy: No retirement is recommended. Optionally use “The name begins with a letter from A to M.” if faster reading is preferred; retain the existing negative form if its mild trickiness is intentional.

findings.problem: This accepted alphabet-half condition is assigned to 63 countries. The final-letter N-to-Z condition appears for six more, and the A-to-M condition for two, so 71 countries receive an alphabet-half clue. This is a concentration observation about variety, not evidence that the clues conflict with the user's preference or should be removed.

evidence.title: Current bank assignments
evidence.supports: Exact assignment counts are 63 for name-first-n-z, six for name-last-n-z, and two for name-first-a-m. The supplied preference permits alphabet-half conditions and rejects first-versus-last comparisons and repeated-letter puzzles.

findings.suggestedPlainLanguageRemedy: Keep these conditions available. If greater variety is desired, distribute other accepted general hints more often without treating alphabet-half clues as disallowed.

findings.problem: Cyprus is a member of this catalog clue under UN M49 Western Asia, while data.js labels its broad region Europe. The Asia-island phrase is not assigned to Cyprus; its actual hints use island status and the Mediterranean coast. The current assignment therefore avoids the conflicting labels. Keep this as a catalog caution before future reuse.

assignedNeighbourAreaComparisons.borderEvidenceLimit: Uses the retained mledoze snapshot border graph, with targeted primary neighbour-set checks in the separate case list. Fresh World Bank data supports the arithmetic; it is not a complete independent primary border audit. Whole-country land area is compared, not the part of a neighbour on the shared island.

wordingScan.note: These were inspected in the current catalog rather than inferred from previous drafts. Alphabet-half conditions are accepted by the user; their frequency is a variety observation only.

limitations: Zero established false claims is a bounded result, not proof that all 390 assigned geographic statements have exhaustive independent primary support.

Most ordinary border memberships were checked against the retained upstream snapshot and known geography. Only the listed edge cases received fresh targeted primary checks; international boundary history was not comprehensively researched.
Ocean/region/island memberships were assessed with explicit attention to the actual phrase. A defensible stored convention can still mislead a player if the short text hides it.
The UN M49 check validates statistical country groupings, not exclusive physical continent membership. Russia, Türkiye, Kazakhstan and Egypt require care when interpreting any-territory geography.
FAO coast sources are older stable geography documents. Direct retrieval of some UN map/PDF sources was blocked; indexed source descriptions were used and are labelled in the evidence.
Inactive catalog examples are labelled separately and must not be counted as errors in today's selected hints.
Suggested replacements are review recommendations only. Their final assignment and usefulness, including candidate counts and combined giveaways, have not been playtested or implemented.

playerPreferenceInterpretation.accepted: Basic alphabet-half conditions are accepted. The user explicitly proposed “First letter not from second half of alphabet” and requested basic, mildly wicked general hints.
rejected: Comparing the first and last letters alphabetically
playerPreferenceInterpretation.assessmentConsequence: Do not recommend retiring alphabet-half conditions on taste grounds. Clearer A–M wording is optional editorial polish; frequency can be discussed as a variety observation.

assessmentCorrections.reason: Corrected an unsupported interpretation of the user's player preferences after clarification. The user proposed alphabet-half clues and rejected first-versus-last comparisons and repeated-letter puzzles.
assessmentCorrections.effect: Removed taste-based retirement recommendations, made A–M phrasing optional low-priority polish, and retained frequency as an informational variety observation. Geographic findings and checked facts are unchanged.
